evidence.approach: entangling QNN head for OOD generalization
evidence.reason: OOD AUC is at/below chance and one QNN arm collapses to a single predicted class

evidence.approach: post-hoc OOD threshold sweep as a usable decision rule
evidence.reason: post-hoc sweep yields no operating point that improves on chance with non-degenerate recall

observations.value: Thresholds sweep the saved model's own OOD probabilities; no labels were used to fit weights, only to select a reported operating point. This is post-hoc analysis, not a claim of improved generalization.

evidence.reason: noisy quantum-kernel accuracies equal the classical oracle at every recorded sigma and retention falls below the required floor

evidence.approach: qubit/layer/encoding ablation as evidence of improvement
evidence.reason: three configurations were measured but n is below the recommended minimum and the accuracy CI spans chance

acceptance.criterion: A primary-model gain must exceed a control-noise margin of two control SDs.
Quantum advantage requires a positive paired difference, Holm p below alpha, a CI excluding zero, and power at the required minimum.
A matched classical control must reproduce the gain at the required n before any quantum mechanism is credited.
Every QNN OOD arm must exceed chance accuracy and chance AUC.
The QNN must emit non-degenerate predictions for every dataset class.
A reported threshold must beat chance with balanced recall and precision at least half of chance (chance derived from the class count).
A noise-robustness claim requires a quantum/classical gap at a recorded sigma and accuracy retention at the required floor.
Architecture ablations need the recommended sample size and an accuracy CI excluding chance.
A quantum run must not fall back to a classical oracle.
Every compared aggregate must carry n, ddof=1 SD, full values and a CI.
No comparison may be labelled significant below the minimum paired n.
Every declared ablation configuration must report a run.
